note: Raw Phase 3A extraction layer. Same records as _exports/phase3/ with no interpretation added. Regenerated - do not hand-edit. Contains NO interview data and no synthetic output.
extract_method: pypdf 6.x text-layer extraction over the published PDF, downloaded with a browser UA. No OCR was used. These are browser-printed PDFs and some characters are lost to font-encoding (notably ligatures: 'Verified' -> 'Veri ed', 'Findings' -> 'Find ngs'). Numeric values survive; this matters for blanks-vs-zeros but not for the counts used here.

forms.note: Largest measured form. 16 recognised startups lose their identity between the DPIIT table and the TRL table.
Near-complete join (4 lost). Three malformed placeholder DPIIT values appear, i.e. the operator left the field unfilled but the table still demanded a key.
REVERSE GAP: the TRL table carries a DPIIT number for an innovation whose startup is not in the recognised table. Same-document contradiction between two tables of one submission.
Clean join. Small denominator, so a single good data-entry operator can hold the whole thing together - which is itself the point.
WORST measured rate: 4 of 6 (67%) drop. A small NIT can recognise 6 startups but can only evidence a TRL for 2, because it does not hold the other 4 founders' DPIIT numbers.
Private college. Clean join on a tiny denominator.

forms.contradiction: Records 0 IIC stars for 2020-21 and leaves 2019-20 BLANK, while running one of India's most mature technology business incubators. The recorded value contradicts the institution's own published capability, so 0 is a non-report, not a measurement.
Section 1.2 records '1,2,3,4' in a single cell for 2018-19: four distinct values in one scalar field, so the cell cannot be parsed as a number.
Same multi-value cell defect as IIT (ISM), and the highest no-data count in the set (7) from the smallest institution.

verbatim.text: are Recorded in the YUKTI National Innovation Repository of the IIC
verbatim.meaning: ARIIA Section 4 does not ask the institution to hold a TRL. It asks how many innovations are VERIFIED AND RECOMMENDED, and defers the record itself to YUKTI-NIR, a central IIC system. The institution is a pointer, not a system of record.

verbatim.text: Total no. of Innovations (Verified and Recommended) in Different TRLs (4-9)
verbatim.meaning: The institution submits a COUNT that it cannot independently verify. 'Verified and Recommended' is done centrally.

verbatim.text: Existence of IPR Cell / Patent Facilitation Unit / Technology Transfer
verbatim.meaning: ARIIA 3.3 asks whether an IPR CELL EXISTS. It is a yes/no capability checkbox. It is NOT a patent lifecycle and it does not record a single patent number.

verbatim.text: Start-ups/Ventures Established and Supported at HEI and Recognitions Received
verbatim.meaning: Section 5 records that a venture was STARTED and SUPPORTED, plus recognitions received. Supported is unquantified: no amount, no date, no scope of support.
The performance metric is a 1-5 ordinal STAR BAND awarded by the central IIC body, not a continuous innovation score.

verbatim.text: Institute Own/Internal  |  Number of External Sponsorship/External
verbatim.meaning: ARIIA forces an EXPENDITURE split between own money and external sponsorship. It is spend already committed, not a funding source, and not a budget the applicant is asking for.
A blank and a 0 sit in the SAME column of the SAME table for consecutive years. Two different sentinels for the same condition, with no legend distinguishing them.

limits: Nothing here is interview evidence. Willingness to pay, felt pain and actual budget ownership remain unverified.
The corpus is 11 forms from institutions that CHOOSE to publish. IICs that do not publish are absent, so missingness within this set understates the real gap.
Extraction is a text layer only, with no OCR. Ligature loss affects wording but not the counts used in F-DPIIT-JOIN.
Join-key counts are distinct DPIIT numbers per table. A single startup with several innovations can appear more than once in the TRL table, so dpiit_in_trl is a key count, not a startup count.
Only one ARIIA form (LBRCE 2020) exposes the fund-split rows in a readable layout; the 2022 forms use a newer template whose column labels the text layer does not preserve.
Years are not comparable across the two forms (see F-ARIYA-AY), so no cross-form total is computed anywhere in this module.
